title: Neocortical long-range inhibition promotes cortical synchrony and sleep.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: Nature version is not open access, has no PMCID, and no supplement, accessions or repository hits. I read the full text of the bioRxiv preprint (PMC11213009, 2024.06.20.599756) and found no data availability statement. The only data links are to public Allen Brain Observatory data and the Allen Brain Knowledge Platform, plus code packages (allensdk, buzcode, suite2p, facemap). Searched Zenodo, DANDI (0 hits for 'Chodl'), Figshare and Dryad (0 hits) and found no deposit from this study.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Preprint figure legend: N = 15 mice, n = 97 Sst-Chodl cells imaged (68 recorded across both sleep and wake), 42 cell pairs. Also from the preprint: optogenetic stimulation with LFP (local field potential) and single-unit recordings, and DeepLabCut tracking of nesting behaviour. I could not read the Nature version's data availability statement (paywalled; publisher scraping is not allowed).

a1_downloadable.note: No deposited dataset found. The preprint has no data availability statement, the Nature text is paywalled, and Zenodo, DANDI, Figshare and Dryad searches returned nothing. Materials go through the corresponding author, which in practice means 'on request'.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked in files because none exist. Sleep and wake state labels would come from the authors' own scoring of LFP, EMG (muscle activity) and pupil data. No table of those labels has been shared.

a5_enough_rows.note: Per the preprint text only: 97 imaged cells from 15 mice. The real unit for generalising is the mouse (15), far below the threshold. Time-binned epochs would be many, but they are not independent across animals.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Raw two-photon imaging and Neuropixels-style electrophysiology would be large, and none of it is deposited.

a8_label_provenance.note: State labels would be thresholds on delta/theta power and EMG, i.e. computed from the same signals a model would use as features. That makes the label circular by construction.

existing_models.name: SleepEns (time-series ensemble sleep-stage classifier for mice, SLEEP 2023)
existing_models.score_and_split: About 90% agreement with expert scorers on four states (active wake, quiet wake, NREM (non-rapid-eye-movement) sleep, REM sleep); split details not checked.

existing_models.name: Transformer model for real-time classification of cortical slow-wave states (Neuroscience Research 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Abstract reports high accuracy; numbers and split not retrieved.

backbone.name: none suitable (no open freeze-and-head backbone for two-photon calcium imaging or LFP in the listed set)

integration.partner_dataset: Allen Brain Observatory Visual Coding (public two-photon imaging of Sst cells, with running and pupil state)
integration.join_key: none (different animals; it could only be pooled by cell type)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Can the arousal state of a mouse be decoded from rare Sst-Chodl cells better than from the general Sst population? This cannot be tested without the study's own data.

controls.external_validation: Allen Brain Observatory Sst imaging (public), but only for the broad Sst population

honest_claim_h3: With 97 cells from 15 mice, at most: 'In head-fixed mice from one lab, Sst-Chodl calcium activity separates slow-wave sleep from movement.' The paper already shows this with statistics, not ML.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the activity of rare long-range inhibitory brain cells to predict whether a mouse is asleep, resting or moving.
plain_idea.train_on: Time windows of calcium-imaging activity from Sst-Chodl neurons (a rare class of inhibitory cells) plus cortical field potentials. The paper reports 97 cells in 15 mice; I verified no files.
plain_idea.predict: Behavioural state per time window (slow-wave sleep, quiet wake, movement, REM sleep), scored by the authors from LFP (local field potential) power, muscle activity and pupil size.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Sleep researchers would learn whether this rare cell type alone tracks arousal. But the data is not shared, and the states are defined from the same signals a model would use.

more_or_better_data.why: No data is accessible. The paper reports 15 mice, against the multi-animal EEG/LFP (brain-wave) corpora used by SleepEns-type scorers.

confidence_score.why: No data to estimate noise from.

models_beatable.why: Mouse sleep-scoring classifiers already reach about 90% agreement with experts (SleepEns, 2023). There is little headroom, and no data here to test on.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No accessible data joins to this paper, so no condition holds.

ml_idea: Decode sleep/wake state from Sst-Chodl calcium activity, holding out whole mice. This is not feasible: the data is not deposited, n = 15 mice, and the state labels come from the same LFP features.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because no data is available.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Find a deposited dataset (DANDI, Zenodo, Figshare, Dryad). Done: none found.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: no deposited data was found (the preprint has no data availability statement, the Nature text is paywalled, and four repository searches came up empty). It would also fail A5 (15 mice, 97 cells) and A8 (sleep states are defined from the same LFP signals a model would use).
